value.body: Statisticians design surveys and studies and apply statistical methods to analyse the data. They work in government statistical offices, research institutes, pharma and clinical research, insurance, market research and analytics teams, and the day involves sampling, data cleaning, modelling and writing up results.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc in Statistics or Mathematics

items.label: Government route
items.value: Indian Statistical Service via the UPSC ISS exam; SSC Statistical Investigator posts

value.title: How you get in
value.body: With a bachelor's degree, freshers often start as data or analytics associates; most statistician titles ask for an M.Sc in Statistics. Government posts come through UPSC's Indian Statistical Service exam (needs a statistics-related master's or degree with statistics) or SSC exams.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Programming in R, SAS or Python

value.title: At a glance
items: A master's degree is common for statistician titles.
Common next steps: senior statistician, biostatistician, data scientist or actuarial routes.
Clinical-research roles often require knowledge of SAS.
